headline: NWS has issued a Coastal Flood Warning for the Bay shoreline from 6 AM Monday through Thursday's king tides; rain before then stays light, with no flooding burst in any model through Monday.

summary.text: New since this morning: a Coastal Flood Warning (up to 3 ft inundation near shorelines and tidal waterways) from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM Thursday. The advisory now runs until 6 AM Monday.
Wettest 3 hours, next 72 h: HRRR 0.10, RRFS 0.10, GFS 0.10, NBM 0.05, ECMWF 0.05 in. Consensus about 0.10 in (0.08 this morning). All models agree it stays light.
No street flooding expected through Monday. Yellow (garage) needs about 0.71 in in 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour; the models are far below that.
Light rain Saturday evening into early Sunday, peaking around 8 PM to midnight. Scattered showers possible Sunday afternoon and evening. Monday dry. Heavier storm Tuesday into Wednesday.
Tides running about 1.5 ft above prediction. Saturday's rain falls on the rising tide toward the lower 6.6 ft evening high. Channel low: 0.24 ft at Alameda, 0.11 ft at Caltrain.
Nothing needed tonight or Saturday. By Monday evening: clear street drain grates and yard drains, check sandbags, and plan where cars go for Tuesday.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: This morning's shower bands have moved down the Central Coast, and tonight is cold and mostly clear (NWS San Francisco, 2:33 PM). The second system in the series brushes the Bay Area Saturday evening as a fairly progressive band, with post-frontal showers lingering Sunday; NWS expects 0.1 to 0.5 in region-wide, highest in the coastal ranges, and notes that a strong convective cell on Sunday could locally raise totals. Monday is the dry day. A stronger system arrives Tuesday morning and continues into early Wednesday, with more significant rain and wind, during the king tide cycle. That storm is still beyond the models in this snapshot, which end late Monday.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
The main change since the 10:25 AM discussion is the coastal flood product: NWS upgraded the Bays to a Coastal Flood Warning from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM Thursday and extended the Coastal Flood Advisory to 6 AM Monday.

Rain guidance changed little. Wettest 3 hours / total in the next 72 hours:
• HRRR (2 PM Fri run): 0.10 / 0.20 in through the end of its run Sunday morning, with its wettest hour (0.07 in) Saturday evening around 8 PM. The 15-minute output agrees: 0.02 in per 15 minutes for an hour Saturday evening, then again around 11 PM.
• RRFS (4 AM Fri run): 0.10 / 0.29 in, but its wettest 3 hours come Sunday evening (5 to 8 PM), from post-frontal showers, plus some Sunday afternoon.
• GFS 0.10 / 0.21 in, NBM 0.05 / 0.17 in, ECMWF 0.05 / 0.14 in, all Saturday night.

Consensus (HRRR 0.10 × 1.25, RRFS 0.10, NBM 0.05): about 0.10 in, up slightly from 0.08 in. Even allowing for HRRR's history of under-forecasting bursts by about 3×, Saturday night would stay under 0.40 in in 3 hours. RRFS's Sunday showers are the kind of cell NWS mentions; a single strong one is the only way this weekend gets interesting, and no model shows it.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model keeps running about 1.5 ft above the predicted tides. Tonight's 6.4 ft high at 9:15 PM runs about 8.1 ft. Saturday's 8.4 ft high at 9:06 AM runs about 9.9 ft, before the rain. Saturday's rain arrives after the 0.3 ft low at 4:05 PM (about 1.5 ft on the model) and falls on the rising tide toward the 6.6 ft high at 10:19 PM (about 8.2 ft), so drainage slows somewhat late in the evening, but the amounts are small. The model run ends 7 AM Sunday, so Sunday's 8.8 ft high at 9:42 AM and Monday's 9.2 ft high at 10:20 AM are not covered yet.

The Coastal Flood Warning describes high tides at San Francisco running 2.1 ft above normal Sunday, 2.3 ft Monday, 2.9 ft Tuesday and 3.0 ft Wednesday, including up to 1.8 ft of surge, with up to 3 ft of inundation in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the street, the concern is mostly the overlap with Tuesday and Wednesday rain: high tides with surge slow the channel's drainage.

Channel: at Alameda de las Pulgas it reads 0.24 ft at 3 PM (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft). Upstream of Caltrain the last reading in the feed is 0.11 ft at 11:50 AM (Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft); that reading is about four hours old.

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry since this morning. The Caltrain rain gauge's last tip was at 7:45 AM: nothing in the last 6 hours and 0.20 in over 24 hours. Both channel gauges are low and steady.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Low for this weekend: all five models keep the wettest 3 hours at 0.10 in or less. The main uncertainty is a stray convective shower Sunday, which RRFS hints at. Tuesday's storm is not yet in this snapshot's models, so its timing and intensity, and how it lines up with the late-morning king tides, will come in the next discussions.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• No need to move cars this weekend.
• Before Tuesday (Monday is the dry day NWS recommends for this): clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains, check sandbags, and decide where cars will go if Tuesday's rain lands near a high tide.
• Stay away from the Bay shore and tidal sloughs at the morning high tides; don't walk or drive through moving water.
